title: Martin Luther as an Augustinian monk
creator: Lucas Cranach the Elder (engraving)
why_public_domain: Engraved in 1520 by Lucas Cranach the Elder, who died in 1553. Reproduced in a book.
original_holder: Johan Huizinga, Erasmus and the Age of Reformation (Harper Torchbook ed., 1957), plate XXI, via Project Gutenberg #22900; the plate list gives "Engraving by Lucas Cranach. 1520"
caption: Luther in his friar's cowl, engraved by Cranach the year before Worms. The Latin verse below says that Luther's own works show his undying mind and Cranach's wax shows only his mortal face. The date 'M.D.XX' (1520) is at the foot.

title: Portrait of Cardinal Girolamo (Hieronymus) Aleander
creator: Unknown artist (drawing in the Recueil d'Arras)
why_public_domain: A 16th-century drawing by an unknown artist. Reproduced in a book.
original_holder: Huizinga, Erasmus and the Age of Reformation (1957), plate XXIV, via Project Gutenberg #22900; the original drawing is in the Recueil d'Arras, Bibliothèque municipale, Arras
caption: Girolamo Aleander, the papal nuncio who argued the case against Luther at Worms and drafted the edict that condemned him. In this pen portrait he wears a cleric's cap. He became a cardinal later, in 1538.

title: Charles V at the Battle of Mühlberg
creator: Titian
date: 1548 (photograph by Braun, Clément & Cie; reproduced c. 1904)
why_public_domain: Painted in 1548 by Titian, who died in 1576. Reproduced from an early photograph in a book printed in the early 1900s.
original_holder: Claude Phillips, The Later Work of Titian, via Project Gutenberg #12657; the painting is in the Museo del Prado, Madrid
caption: Charles V in armour, riding with a lance. Titian painted him in 1548, twenty-seven years after Worms, to mark his victory over the Protestant princes at Mühlberg. At Worms in 1521 he was twenty-one.

title: Self-portrait of Albrecht Dürer
creator: Albrecht Dürer
why_public_domain: Painted in 1500 by Albrecht Dürer, who died in 1528. Reproduced in a book printed in 1899.
original_holder: Jennie Ellis Keysor, Great Artists, Vol. 1 (1899), via Project Gutenberg #22564; the painting is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich
caption: Dürer's frontal self-portrait of 1500, with long curls and a fur collar. In May 1521, while travelling in the Netherlands, he heard that Luther had been seized after Worms and wrote a long lament for him in his journal.

title: Portrait of Ulrich von Hutten
creator: Unknown German woodcutter
why_public_domain: A woodcut by an unknown German artist from the early 16th century. Reproduced in a book.
original_holder: Huizinga, Erasmus and the Age of Reformation (1957), plate XXII ("Anonymous German woodcut"), via Project Gutenberg #22900
caption: Ulrich von Hutten, a knight and humanist, in armour under a laurel wreath, holding a sword. In 1521 he sided with Luther and sent threatening letters to the papal envoys at Worms. The exact date of the woodcut is not given.

title: Akbar holding a religious assembly (Jesuits at Akbar's court)
creator: Mughal court painter, from a manuscript of the Akbarnama
why_public_domain: A Mughal painting made around 1605. OpenStax credits it as public domain, by way of the Chester Beatty Library.
original_holder: Chester Beatty Library, Dublin; via OpenStax World History, Volume 2, fig. "Emperor Akbar" (panel a)
caption: Akbar sits under a red canopy at night, hearing scholars of several faiths. The two men in black at left are Jesuit priests from Goa. The debates in the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri began in 1575.

title: Akbar and the Jesuits (detail)
creator: Mughal court painter, from a manuscript of the Akbarnama
why_public_domain: A detail of a Mughal painting made around 1605. OpenStax credits it as public domain, by way of the Chester Beatty Library.
original_holder: Chester Beatty Library, Dublin; via OpenStax World History, Volume 2, fig. "Emperor Akbar" (panel b, detail)
caption: A closer view of the same painting. Akbar, in yellow with an orange turban, gestures toward a scholar in white. The two Jesuits kneel at left, and books lie open on the carpet between them.

title: Akbar directing the tying-up of a wild elephant
creator: Mughal court painters, from the Akbarnama manuscript
why_public_domain: A Mughal manuscript painting from about 1590. Reproduced from a photograph in a book printed in 1909.
original_holder: Richard von Garbe, Akbar, Emperor of India (Open Court, 1909), frontispiece, via Project Gutenberg #14134; the book credits the original in "the India Museum" (now the Victoria and Albert Museum, London)
caption: A page from the Akbarnama, the official history of Akbar's reign: men struggle to rope a wild elephant while the emperor directs them. The reproduction is black and white.

title: Akbar, Emperor of India
creator: Unknown artist, after a Mughal portrait
why_public_domain: First printed as the frontispiece of Count Noer's Kaiser Akbar (1880–85) and reproduced in 1909. The engraver is unknown.
original_holder: Garbe, Akbar, Emperor of India (1909), via Project Gutenberg #14134; the book's caption reads 'From Noer's Kaiser Akbar, (Frontispiece to Vol. II)'
caption: Akbar in an oval frame, wearing a jewelled turban and pearls and holding a flower, in the manner of Mughal court portraits. This is a 19th-century European engraving of a Mughal likeness, not a Mughal original.

title: Independence Hall, Philadelphia, 1776
creator: Unknown engraver
date: Engraving published 1899, showing the building as it looked around 1776
why_public_domain: Published in 1899.
original_holder: John T. Morse Jr., Benjamin Franklin (American Statesmen, Standard Library Edition, Houghton, Mifflin, 1899), frontispiece, via Project Gutenberg #21348
caption: The Pennsylvania State House, later called Independence Hall, with its steeple and wing buildings, as it appeared in the Revolutionary years. The Federal Convention met in its east room from May to September 1787.

title: Back of the State House, Philadelphia
creator: William Russell Birch & Son (engraving)
why_public_domain: Engraved around 1800 by William Birch, who died in 1834, and his son Thomas Birch, who died in 1851.
original_holder: From Birch's Views of Philadelphia (1800), via OpenStax / Bill of Rights Institute, Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness (fig. BRI_APUSH_04_04, panel b). The plate is inscribed 'Drawn Engraved & Published by W. Birch & Son'
caption: The State House seen from its walled yard, with walkers under young trees. The delegates' windows looked onto this yard during the closed-door summer of 1787.

title: Congress Voting Independence
creator: Robert Edge Pine, completed by Edward Savage
why_public_domain: Painted between about 1784 and 1801. Pine died in 1788 and Savage in 1817.
original_holder: Historical Society of Pennsylvania; via OpenStax / Bill of Rights Institute, Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness (fig. BRI_APUSH_03_02)
caption: The Assembly Room of the State House, painted with care by an artist who worked in Philadelphia in the 1780s. The scene is the July 1776 vote, but it is the same room where the Convention sat eleven years later.

title: The Constitution of the United States, page one
creator: Constitutional Convention (engrossed by Jacob Shallus)
why_public_domain: US government work. The engrossed and signed original is held by the US National Archives.
original_holder: US National Archives, Washington, DC; this copy is from the 2007 Wikipedia for Schools selection (Wikispeedia dataset), whose file page credits archives.gov
caption: The first of the four parchment pages, beginning 'We the People' in large script. It is the engrossed copy the delegates signed on 17 September 1787. At this size the body text is too small to read.

title: Portrait of Benjamin Franklin
creator: David Martin
why_public_domain: Painted in 1767 by David Martin, who died in 1797.
original_holder: White House collection (a version is also at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts); via Standard Ebooks' cover for The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin, credited in its colophon
caption: Franklin in London at sixty-one, reading with his thumb under his chin and a bust of Isaac Newton behind him. At the Convention twenty years later he was eighty-one, its oldest delegate.

title: James Madison
creator: Gilbert Stuart
why_public_domain: Painted around 1805–07 by Gilbert Stuart, who died in 1828.
original_holder: Via OpenStax / Bill of Rights Institute, Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness (fig. BRI_APUSH_04_03)
caption: Madison in his fifties, seated beside a red drape. At the Convention in 1787 he was thirty-six, and the notes he took every day are the fullest record of its debates. This is a low-resolution copy, 375 pixels wide.

title: The Congress of Vienna
creator: After Jean-Baptiste Isabey (hand-coloured engraving)
why_public_domain: Drawn in 1815 by Jean-Baptiste Isabey, who died in 1855. The engraving was published in 1819. OpenStax credits it as public domain.
original_holder: OpenStax World History, Volume 2, fig. "The Congress of Vienna" (credited to Wikimedia Commons, public domain)
caption: The plenipotentiaries gathered round a table in a panelled room. Isabey drew the scene for Talleyrand. Wellington stands at far left in profile, and Castlereagh sits at centre with his legs crossed.

title: Prince Metternich
creator: Unknown engraver
why_public_domain: An early 19th-century portrait engraving, published in 1902.
original_holder: Comte A. de La Garde-Chambonas, Anecdotal Recollections of the Congress of Vienna (London: Chapman & Hall, 1902), facing p. 352, via Project Gutenberg #54061
caption: Klemens von Metternich, the Austrian foreign minister who hosted the Congress, seated sideways in an armchair in court dress, wearing his orders.

title: Charles Maurice de Talleyrand
creator: Unknown engraver, after François Gérard
why_public_domain: An engraving after a portrait by François Gérard, who died in 1837. Published in 1902.
original_holder: La Garde-Chambonas, Anecdotal Recollections of the Congress of Vienna (1902), facing p. 376, via Project Gutenberg #54061
caption: Talleyrand, France's envoy, seated at a writing desk in the pose of Gérard's full-length portrait, with his signature below. At Vienna he won the defeated French a seat at the table.

title: Robert, Viscount Castlereagh, Marquess of Londonderry
creator: Unknown engraver, probably after Sir Thomas Lawrence
why_public_domain: An early 19th-century portrait engraving, published in 1902.
original_holder: La Garde-Chambonas, Anecdotal Recollections of the Congress of Vienna (1902), facing p. 280, via Project Gutenberg #54061
caption: Castlereagh, the British foreign secretary, standing with one hand on a table. He led Britain's delegation at Vienna until Wellington took his place in February 1815.

title: Alexander I, Emperor of Russia
creator: Unknown engraver
why_public_domain: An early 19th-century portrait engraving, published in 1902.
original_holder: La Garde-Chambonas, Anecdotal Recollections of the Congress of Vienna (1902), facing p. 142, via Project Gutenberg #54061
caption: Tsar Alexander I in uniform with a sash and star. He came to Vienna in person and pressed hard for a Polish kingdom under Russia.

title: Francis I, Emperor of Austria
creator: Unknown engraver
why_public_domain: An early 19th-century portrait engraving, published in 1902.
original_holder: La Garde-Chambonas, Anecdotal Recollections of the Congress of Vienna (1902), frontispiece, via Project Gutenberg #54061
caption: Emperor Francis I of Austria, seated in a palace interior in a white uniform. He was host to the Congress and paid for its long round of balls and festivities.

title: Elizabeth Cady Stanton with two of her sons
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: A photograph taken in 1848 by an unknown photographer.
original_holder: Via OpenStax / Bill of Rights Institute, Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness (fig. BRI_APUSH_06_03, panel a); the original holder is not stated there
caption: Stanton, aged about thirty-two, holding two small sons. This is the year she drafted the Declaration of Sentiments at Seneca Falls, where she was raising her children.

title: Lucretia Mott
creator: Joseph Kyle
why_public_domain: Painted in 1842 by Joseph Kyle, who died in 1863.
original_holder: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution; via OpenStax / Bill of Rights Institute, Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness (fig. BRI_APUSH_06_03, panel b)
caption: Mott in Quaker cap and white shawl, six years before Seneca Falls. Her visit to the Finger Lakes in July 1848 was the reason the convention was called.

title: Elizabeth Cady Stanton (with autograph)
creator: Unknown engraver
why_public_domain: Published in 1881.
original_holder: Stanton, Anthony and Gage, eds., History of Woman Suffrage, Vol. I (1881), via Project Gutenberg #28020
caption: Stanton in later life, in an engraved portrait with her signature. The History of Woman Suffrage, which she co-edited, preserves the Seneca Falls proceedings and the Declaration of Sentiments.

title: Lucretia Mott (with autograph)
creator: Unknown engraver
why_public_domain: Published in 1881.
original_holder: History of Woman Suffrage, Vol. I (1881), via Project Gutenberg #28020
caption: Lucretia Mott in old age, in a bonnet and shawl, signed 'affecty. thine, Lucretia Mott'.

title: Martha C. Wright (with autograph)
creator: Unknown engraver
why_public_domain: Published in 1881.
original_holder: History of Woman Suffrage, Vol. I (1881), via Project Gutenberg #28020
caption: Martha Coffin Wright, Lucretia Mott's younger sister, in a white cap. She was one of the five women who planned the Seneca Falls convention over tea in July 1848.

title: Frederick Douglass
creator: Unknown American artist
why_public_domain: Painted around 1844 by an unknown artist.
original_holder: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution (as usually credited); via Standard Ebooks' cover for Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, credited in its colophon
caption: Douglass as a young man, aged about twenty-six, in a dark coat and white stock. Four years later he was the only African American known to have attended the Seneca Falls convention, and he spoke there for the resolution on the vote.

title: Frederick Douglass (frontispiece portrait)
creator: Augustus Robin (engraving)
why_public_domain: Published in 1881.
original_holder: Frederick Douglass, Life and Times of Frederick Douglass (Hartford, 1881), frontispiece, via Project Gutenberg #71893
caption: Douglass in his sixties with his white beard and hair, signed 'Fred'k Douglass'. In Life and Times he recalled with pride that he had backed the call for the vote at Seneca Falls.

title: Abolition of the Slave Trade: public meeting of delegates held at Freemasons' Hall, June 1840
creator: Lithograph after Benjamin Robert Haydon
why_public_domain: A print made around 1840–41 after Haydon's painting. Haydon died in 1846.
original_holder: OpenStax / Bill of Rights Institute, Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness (fig. BRI_APUSH_06_03, attributed there to John Alfred Vinter); the inscription reads "After the original picture by Haydon"
caption: The World Anti-Slavery Convention in London, June 1840, with Thomas Clarkson in the chair. Women delegates, among them Lucretia Mott, were refused seats on the floor. There Mott and Stanton first met and resolved to hold a convention of their own.

title: The Signing of Peace in the Hall of Mirrors, Versailles, 28th June 1919
creator: William Orpen
why_public_domain: Painted in 1919 by William Orpen, who died in 1931. Reproduced in his own book in 1921.
original_holder: William Orpen, An Onlooker in France 1917–1919 (Williams and Norgate, 1921), plate LI 'Signing the Peace Treaty', via Project Gutenberg #20215; the painting is in the Imperial War Museum, London
caption: Orpen's painting of the treaty signing. The Allied leaders sit in a row at a long table under the tall mirrored arches, and a German delegate signs in the foreground. The reproduction is black and white.

title: A Peace Conference at the Quai d'Orsay
creator: William Orpen
why_public_domain: Painted in 1919 by William Orpen, who died in 1931. Reproduced in 1921.
original_holder: Orpen, An Onlooker in France 1917–1919 (1921), plate LXXXIII 'A Meeting of the Peace Conference', via Project Gutenberg #20215; the painting is in the Imperial War Museum, London
caption: The delegates in session in the Salle de l'Horloge at the French foreign ministry, dwarfed by the marble chimneypiece and its statue. The gilded room takes up most of the picture and the statesmen sit small along its foot.

title: The Council of Four: Lloyd George, Orlando, Clemenceau and Wilson
creator: Edward N. Jackson, U.S. Army Signal Corps (as usually credited)
why_public_domain: Published in 1919. It is usually credited to Edward N. Jackson of the US Army Signal Corps, which would also make it a US government work.
original_holder: US National Archives (as usually credited); via OpenStax U.S. History, fig. 23.4 (no credit given there)
caption: From left: David Lloyd George, Vittorio Orlando, Georges Clemenceau and Woodrow Wilson, the four men who settled the main terms of peace in private talks, standing outside a doorway in Paris. This is a low-resolution copy, 390 pixels wide.

title: President Woodrow Wilson
creator: William Orpen
why_public_domain: Painted in 1919 by William Orpen, who died in 1931. Reproduced in 1921.
original_holder: Orpen, An Onlooker in France 1917–1919 (1921), plate XLVI, via Project Gutenberg #20215
caption: Wilson seated, painted from life by Orpen in Paris during the conference. Orpen wrote that the president arrived "smiling as usual" and laughed at his stories.

title: The Marquis Saionji
creator: William Orpen
why_public_domain: Painted in 1919 by William Orpen, who died in 1931. Reproduced in 1921.
original_holder: Orpen, An Onlooker in France 1917–1919 (1921), plate XLVII ('The Marquis Siongi' in the book), via Project Gutenberg #20215
caption: Saionji Kinmochi, head of Japan's delegation, in a dark suit. His delegation proposed a clause on racial equality for the League of Nations Covenant, and the conference refused it.

title: Mr. Lloyd George, President Wilson and M. Clemenceau
creator: William Orpen
why_public_domain: Drawn in 1919 by William Orpen, who died in 1931. Reproduced in 1921.
original_holder: Orpen, An Onlooker in France 1917–1919 (1921), plate LXXXII, via Project Gutenberg #20215
caption: A quick sketch of three heads close together, the peacemakers in conference, drawn by the official painter at the conference.

title: Georges Clemenceau, 1918
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: An anonymous photograph published in 1919.
original_holder: H. M. Hyndman, Clemenceau: The Man and His Time (London: Grant Richards, 1919), frontispiece, via Project Gutenberg #60036
caption: Clemenceau, the French premier, in his late seventies, the year before he presided over the peace conference.

title: 'Big Three' met at Yalta
creator: U.S. Army Signal Corps photographer
why_public_domain: US government work. The photograph was taken by the US Army Signal Corps and is held in the US National Archives.
original_holder: US National Archives (Army Signal Corps Collection); via OpenStax World History, Volume 2, fig. "The Big Three"
caption: Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin seated in the courtyard of Livadia Palace, with their military and diplomatic staffs standing behind them. Roosevelt, two months before his death, wears a cape over his shoulders.
